structured_output.what_is_happening: AR Dogy (DOGY) is a pump.fun coin about 3.3 hours old, still on the bonding curve (~92 of ~115 virtual SOL). It is named after a real TikTok AR effect/app called "AR Dogy", which puts a goofy virtual dog into your camera view. Over 6h it rose about 600% to roughly $30k mcap on about $154k volume, then topped near $40k (ATH price 4.0e-5). At trigger time it was fading: m5 -7.6% on DexScreener, -20% on GeckoTerminal, with 1 unique buyer vs 14 sellers in the last 5 minutes. A re-fetch minutes later showed ~$26.9k mcap, m5 -23.75%, and 8 buys vs 22 sells. The creator has already closed out (creator_close, 0 balance), the coin is flagged as a community takeover, and GMGN tags 174 of 228 traders as bundlers. At least 9 other 'AR Dogy'/DOGY copies were launched the same day, all now dead.

narrative.description: This is a meme coin based on the AR Dogy dog-filter effect on TikTok and Instagram. The meme is real. There are several AR Dogy apps, TikTok discover pages and YouTube shorts. One app has ~370k downloads, 96k of them in the last 30 days. But the TikTok sticker link dates from around March 2026, so this is an ongoing trend, not a breaking event. I found nothing that explains a crypto catalyst today.
narrative.why_spreading: The spread looks like pump.fun trenches rotation, not outside attention. The TikTok meme is recognizable and many deployers launched copies at once. This one won the curve race. I found no X, Reddit or news discussion of the token itself.

token_connection.why_this_token: Among the same-name launches, this is the only one with meaningful liquidity and volume. The others show $0 liquidity and 0 h1 volume. So it is the de facto winner of the copy race. Its only 'official' link is a random X status from commando100x plus the TikTok effect URL, and there is no official brand connection.
token_connection.competing_tokens: At least 9 same-name/ticker coins launched 2026-09-24, e.g. ECd2e9...DV4e, 6Ss1wy..., 8EW3o1..., GUuygE...pump, all dead. There is also an older, unrelated 2024 $DOGY (Solama dev) project.

authenticity.evidence: GMGN tags 174 bundler wallets out of 228 holders, and the top bundler traders hold 34.9%. The bot/degen rate is 54%. RugCheck shows a 4-wallet transfer insider network. The creator has exited and the coin has CTO status. There is no organic social discussion anywhere I could reach. The only social link is an unviewable X status from an unrelated-looking account.
authenticity.uncertainty: I could not read X (HTTP 402). GMGN's bundler tag may be counting pump.fun trading bots. The top 10 holders are fairly spread at about 2-3% each.

structural_risks: Heavy bundler share (34.9% held by top bundler traders) that can dump into the curve
Momentum already reversing: sellers far outnumber buyers in the last 5-15 minutes
Price is ~25-33% below the ATH and needs to reach ~$55-60k mcap from entry to double
Creator exited; CTO with no organized community found

structured_output.counterargument: It is near graduation (92 of 115 SOL). Migrating to PumpSwap often brings a fresh wave of buyers, and the recognizable TikTok meme with 748 holders could fuel a second leg. A double from about $25k to $50k is small in absolute terms for a coin that already did 7x today, and 9 smart wallets plus 1 KOL wallet are in.
unknowns: What the commando100x X post says and how much engagement it has
Whether a TikTok creator or KOL is actively pushing it
The actual entry price 25 minutes after trigger
Whether the bundler wallets are insiders or generic bots

source_coverage.notes: The X status fetch returned 402. The contract-address search gave nothing relevant. Searches for the name only turned up the AR Dogy apps and TikTok pages. The DexScreener API re-fetch shows the price declining after trigger.

structured_output.thesis: A real but not new TikTok meme, with no crypto-specific catalyst. The coin already ran 6-7x, is fading from its ATH with sellers dominating, and is heavily bundled with an exited dev. A further 2x within 6h is unlikely. The more likely paths are bleeding out or a graduation pop that gets sold.
